chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Hammam Ismail ibn Hammam, from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: Verily, supplication and affliction accompany each other until the Day of Judgment. Verily, supplication repels affliction even when it has been firmly decreed.

key_terms.أُبْرِمَ إِبْرَاماً: Firm decree; an absolute infinitive emphasizing the certainty and finality of the ordainment
key_terms.الدُّعَاء: Supplication, invocation, prayer addressed directly to God; a primary act of worship in Islam
key_terms.الْبَلَاء: Affliction, trial, tribulation; a test from God that purifies the believer
key_terms.لَيَتَرَافَقَانِ: They accompany each other; the verb trafaqa implies inseparable companionship on a journey

ai.seo_question: Can supplication (du'a) repel or change divine decree (qada) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (AS), transmitted through Imam al-Rida (AS), teaches that supplication (du'a) and affliction (bala') are inseparably linked companions until the Day of Judgment. This hadith presents a profound theological teaching: du'a can avert divinely ordained trials even after they have been firmly decreed. The phrase 'وَقَدْ أُبْرِمَ إِبْرَاماً' ('even though it has been firmly decreed') addresses the common question of whether supplication can change divine decree, affirming that it can.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Hammam Ismail Bin Hammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The supplication and the affliction would both be together up to the Day of Judgment. The supplication repels the affliction and although it has been strengthened with a strengthening’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from [Ahmad ibn] Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from abu Hammam Isma’Il ibn Hammam from al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) has said, ‘Prayer and pleading before Allah for help, and misfortune are joined together and will remain so until the Day of Judgment. Prayer repeals misfortunes even though it (misfortune) may have already been firmly established.’”
